tools.description: Get fabrication price and delivery offers for a design file or an existing AFN part number. Supports 3D printing, CNC machining, sheet metal, decals, print, and apparel. If the user just provides a file and asks for a price, omit process so AFN can route it to suitable makers. Provide the design as design_file (an attachment or generated file) or file_url (a public URL). For a reorder, pass the UFP part number as part_number instead of a file; locked parts also require share_key from the owner's share link. A .ufp part container is accepted as a design file, and its saved specification applies unless the user changes it. Some offers carry manufacturability_check: the price is set; the shop is confirming it can make the part as drawn (status "checking" for about expected_s seconds, then passed or failed; a status of "repriced" means passed — the price shown is the shop's, never say it changed) — present them as real prices; create_checkout on one that is still checking waits for the shop's answer and never orders a price the shop has not confirmed. Pass instant_only true only when the user wants instant prices without any shop being asked (a demo, a quick look): the quote comes back complete at once, every offer carries its instant price with manufacturability_check.status "unchecked", and nothing on that quote can be checked or ordered — check_offer answers without asking the shop and create_checkout refuses. Quotes made from it with refine_quote, and re-quotes of its .ufp part file, stay instant-only; to order, quote the same part again without instant_only. Pass lazy true when the user wants to look at prices now and have a shop asked only for the offer they pick: no shop is asked to make the quote, it comes back complete at once, and every offer carries our instant price with manufacturability_check.status "unchecked". Unlike instant_only, such a quote CAN be ordered: run check_offer on the offer the user picks (that asks its one shop), and create_checkout once the check passes. A shop we have no instant price for has no offer on a lazy quote — say so if the user asks where a shop is, and quote the part again without lazy to ask every shop. Quotes made from it with refine_quote stay lazy. HOW OLD AN ANSWER IS: a shop's answer is shown for 24 hours, to everyone with the same request (the same design bytes with the same everything asked), so a quote of a part someone priced in the last 24 hours comes back complete at once with those answers and no shop is asked again. An offer says when its shop answered (answered_at). Past 15 minutes it reads stale: true — it is shown at that price and the shop confirms it again before anyone pays (check_offer, or checking out, asks that one shop). A shipping option of such an offer carries eta_approximate: true: say "about N days" from eta_days and never state its eta_date as a date, because no shop stands behind a date until it confirms again. If a quote carries answers_pending, someone else is asking the shops about this same request right now and these are our instant prices: call reopen_quote with that quote_id after retry_after_s seconds. TO PLACE EXACTLY ONE ORDER WITH NO MISTAKES: (1) on get_fabrication_quote list only that shop in vendors and state the pick in selection — the shop, plus the material, finish and shipping speed wanted; (2) read selection_match on the quote: status "one" means exactly one option answers the pick, "many" means say more in the pick (color, thickness, quantity), "none" means nothing on the quote answers it; (3) call create_checkout with quote_id and selection true — it orders that one option at the picked shipping speed, or refuses and creates nothing (selection_not_unique: the pick is not exactly one option; selection_speed_unavailable: the option does not show the picked speed now — an order never takes another speed in its place). It returns the payment link as always: the user pays on that page, nothing is charged without them. An offer whose manufacturability_check reads status "unchecked" with reason "network_restarted" was being confirmed by its shop when the network restarted, so the answer never came: tell the user, in these words, "A new version of AFN has been released, please refresh the page". Nothing is lost — the price stands and the offer can simply be checked again with check_offer. Say it once, when a tool's own text tells you to; the same reason still on an offer on a later read is history, not news.

attachment_urls.description: Additional files for the SAME part — the PDF drawing next to the STEP, spec sheets, BOMs. Pass everything the user gave you; UFP works out which file is the part and which are supporting documents.

bend_count.description: Number of bends in the design (bend lines must be in the file). Prices CNC bending; omit for flat parts

bends.description: Sheet-metal bend lines, each as TWO POINTS in the part's own mm frame (flat DXF parts use z=0: a bend from (0,12.7) to (76.2,12.7) is p1 [0,12.7,0], p2 [76.2,12.7,0]). angle_deg is the target bend angle (90 = a right-angle flange), direction "up"/"down" is the fold direction relative to the flat pattern, radius_mm the requested inside radius (omit it — the shop resolves to its tooling and reports what it used). Pass these when the user articulates WHERE the bends go; a bare "it has 2 bends" is bend_count, not this.

callouts.description: Dimensions you read off the user's drawing that matter ("hole_diameter 6.5mm ±0.1"). The tightest tolerance prunes vendors that cannot hold it.

color.description: ONLY a color the user actually asked for — NEVER pick one for them. fdm_print: Filament color for fdm_print (e.g. black, red); resin_print: Resin color for resin_print (e.g. gray, white, black); powder_print: Powder part color: raw gray/white, or a dye ("black", "dark blue") — vendor-resolved; elastomer_print: Elastomer part color — VCJ parts ship raw; asks resolve with an honest substitution note; cnc: Colour for cnc: with finish anodized it is the anodize colour, otherwise the stock's own colour (black Delrin, clear acrylic). Colour WORDS only; each maker resolves the shade and says what it landed on; laser_cut: Colour of the flat stock for laser_cut (black, clear, natural…). Colour WORDS only; each maker quotes the materials it stocks in that colour and drops the ones that cannot be it; print: Print color ask ("full color", "black and white"). Vendors that only price full color note the substitution; apparel: Garment color for apparel ("black", "heather gray") — vendor-resolved

cut.description: Decal cut style — pass the user's words verbatim ("triangle", "die cut", "circle"). Known: contour|square|oval|kiss_cut; anything else gets closest-match offers with a substitution note. Omit to compare the main options

deadline.description: Latest acceptable delivery date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD

design_data_url.description: Inline design bytes as a data: URL (base64), for MCP clients that cannot pass a file reference

design_file.description: The design file itself (user-attached or generated image/STL). ChatGPT supplies {file_id, download_url} automatically when the user attached a file — just bind the attachment here.

elastomer_finish.description: Elastomer post-processing: as_printed (VCJ parts ship raw — the whole lane today)

elastomer_technology.description: Elastomer process: vapor_cure_jetting (VCJ). Omit to let the vendor pick its default lane for the material

file_url.description: Public URL of the design file — only when the design lives at a URL

finish.description: cnc: CNC surface finish: standard|anodized|polished|bead_blasted (default standard); sheetmetal: as_cut (default) | deburred | anodized | powder_coat — anodized is aluminum-only; powder coat protects mild steel for outdoor use

high_temp.description: Must tolerate sustained heat (vendor heat-resistance claim)

inserts.description: PEM-style hardware inserts pressed into holes of a sheet-metal part — one record per hole. `insert` is the species (nut | flush_nut | standoff | blind_standoff | stud) and `thread` its size ("M4", "1/4-20"); both are required. When known, add length_mm (standoff/stud post length), the hole's center (located_at_mm, part's own mm frame), its axis, the drilled diameter, and `points` — the signed unit vector the insert's functional side faces (flip = negate). Pass these when the user asks for press-in nuts/standoffs/studs; vendors with a hardware service price them.

instant_only.description: true = instant prices only: no shop is asked about the part, now or later on this quote. The quote is complete at once; its offers read "unchecked" and cannot be checked or ordered (routing.instant_only is true on the response). Omit for a regular quote — the only kind that can be ordered

lazy.description: true = our instant prices first, and a shop asked only when the user picks an offer: no shop is asked to make the quote, which is complete at once with every offer "unchecked" (routing.lazy is true on the response). Run check_offer on the offer the user picks — that asks its one shop — and create_checkout once the check passes. A shop we have no instant price for has no offer on such a quote. Omit for a regular quote, which asks the shops now

material.description: ONLY a material the user actually asked for — NEVER guess or default one (a silent "pla" on a bare file drop prunes every maker that does not stock it; OMIT instead and each process quotes across its stocked materials so every maker can bid). fdm_print: pla|petg|asa (free-form — "abs", "polycarbonate" asks resolve to the closest stocked filament with a substitution note); resin_print: standard|tough|high_temp|high_detail resin (free-form asks resolve to the closest supported resin); powder_print: Powder-bed nylon: nylon_12|nylon_12_smooth|nylon_11|nylon_12_gf|nylon_12_esd|nylon_12_white|nylon_pa2200|nylon_12_sls|tpu (free-form — "PA12", "glass filled" resolve to the closest stocked powder); elastomer_print: Jetted elastomer: tepu_30a|tepu_50a (free-form — "TPU", "soft rubber" resolve to the closest stocked durometer); cnc: aluminum_6061|aluminum_7075|stainless_304|titanium|brass|acetal|delrin|abs|nylon_pa6|peek|acrylic (free-form asks resolve to the closest supported stock); sheetmetal: mild_steel|aluminum_5052|stainless_304 (free-form — "steel", "5052", "stainless" resolve; unknown asks get closest-match offers). Omit to compare the defaults; laser_cut: acrylic|plywood|mdf|delrin|uhmw|hdpe|g10|carbon_fiber|mild_steel|aluminum_5052|stainless_304 (free-form — "plexiglass", "birch" resolve; unknown asks get closest-match offers); decal: vinyl|holographic|transparent|glitter (free-form — "chrome" etc. gets closest matches)

materials.description: The materials the user will accept, when they name SEVERAL or a family rather than one ("plastic or metal", "delrin or PLA", "any aluminum") — each word a family ("plastic", "metal", "wood") or a specific material ("pla", "delrin", "aluminum_6061"). Only options in a listed material are shown; which shops are asked does not change. For ONE specific material use material instead: a stated material rules and this list is set aside (the quote says so). Usually OMIT: pass it only when the user names the materials they accept

max_budget_usd.description: Hard budget cap in USD, all-in

metal_alloy.description: Metal AM alloy: stainless_316l|stainless_17_4ph|titanium_ti64|aluminum_alsi10mg|inconel_718|cobalt_chrome|tool_steel_h13|copper (free-form asks like "Ti-6Al-4V" resolve to the closest stocked powder)

metal_finish.description: Metal AM post-processing: as_printed|bead_blast|machined_critical|polished|heat_treated (as_printed keeps support witness marks)

metal_technology.description: Metal AM process: laser_powder_bed (SLM/DMLS/LPBF)|binder_jet|ebm. Omit to let the vendor pick its default for the alloy

min_vendor_reviews.description: Only vendors with at least this many verified-purchase reviews

min_vendor_stars.description: Only vendors whose displayed review rating is at least this many stars (1-5). Vendors with no reviews yet are excluded — the filter demands demonstrated quality

paper.description: Paper stock — free-form ("matte", "glossy", "recycled", "14pt"). Resolved to the closest stock the vendor runs

part_number.description: UFP part number from a previous paid order (UFP-… or part_…). Reorders: replaces design_file/file_url entirely; any other fields provided override the stored spec

placement.description: Print placement for apparel: front (default) | back | front_back

powder_finish.description: Powder post-processing: as_printed (raw powder surface) | vapor_polished | polished

powder_technology.description: Powder process: mjf (HP Multi Jet Fusion) | sls (laser sintering). Omit to let the vendor pick its default lane for the material

process.description: What to fabricate. If the user just drops a file and asks for a price, OMIT this — UFP detects the file type (artwork, mesh — STL/OBJ/PLY/3MF/AMF, BREP — STEP/IGES, DXF) and routes it to every process that can make it; the response's routing.also_possible lists processes UFP can't quote yet

processes.description: Only quote these fabrication processes — a constraint that narrows the auto-routing fan. Friendly terms accepted ("sheet metal", "3d printing", "cnc", "laser"); unmappable terms are reported, never an error. Usually OMIT: auto-routing quotes every process that can make the file. Pass it only when the user explicitly limits the process

product.description: print: Print product kind: business_cards|flyers|posters. Omit to quote every kind the artwork fits; apparel: apparel: t_shirt|hoodie|long_sleeve|tank_top (free-form — "tee", "crewneck" resolve to the closest product)

proven_spec_orders.description: Only vendors with at least N completed orders for this exact process+material — "a vendor that prints PC reliably"

quantities.description: Quantities the user actually wants — pass [1] or [2] if that's the ask. Vendors with a higher minimum quote AT their minimum and the offer notes it (requested_quantity). Default: 25 for decals, 1 for prints; a part_number reorder defaults to the quantity last purchased

requirements.description: Verbatim context terms from the user — materials, finishes, certifications, tolerances ("UV resistant", "anodized: red", "iso 13485", "tolerance: 0.1mm"). UFP applies what it can and reports what it could not; unresolvable terms are logged for vendor sourcing. Do not interrogate the user to fill this — pass what they said.

selection.description: The pick: the ONE option to order, named by what it is rather than by an offer id (ids change when a quote is priced again). vendor = the shop as it appears on offers (friendly names accepted); spec = the resolved options the option must carry, each optional — material, color, finish, thickness_in (leave one out, or null, and it does not narrow the pick); process and quantity likewise optional; shipping_speed = the word the shipping option itself goes by ("standard", "express", "ground"), omitted = the cheapest speed. Storing a pick changes no price and never asks every shop. CHOOSING STARTS THAT ONE SHOP'S CHECK: on a quote you already have, a pick that comes to exactly one option whose shop answered more than 15 minutes ago (or was never asked) has that one shop asked to confirm it, and the answer already says so. Every quote read then carries selection and selection_match { status "one" | "none" | "many", matched, offer_id, shipping_option_id, speed_fallback, confirmed_until, check { state "running" | "fresh" | "not_started", code, retry_after_s }, price_changed }: check "fresh" = the shop's answer is under 15 minutes old; "running" = that shop is being asked now; "not_started" = nobody is being asked and code says why ("ask_limited" = the pick is kept and the shop is asked when the user pays; "quote_expired" = these answers are over 24 hours old: call reopen_quote, the pick is kept). Usually OMIT: pass it when the user has settled on one option, or to order by create_checkout with selection true

share_key.description: Share key for a LOCKED part — the k=… value from the owner's share link (…/part/UFP-…?k=KEY). Required with part_number when the part is locked; omit otherwise

ship_to_zip.description: Destination US ZIP code, exactly as the user stated it. OMIT if the user has not given one — NEVER guess or invent a ZIP. Without it, prices come back all-in with shipping to an assumed central-US destination, flagged on routing.ship_to

ships_from.description: Only vendors that ship from these countries/regions ("only US vendors", "keep it domestic") — an INCLUDE list. Friendly terms accepted ("US", "Europe", "Germany", "China", "UK"); unmappable terms are reported, never an error. Vendors whose origin is unknown or whose network is worldwide (origin not guaranteed) are excluded, each with a note saying why. Usually OMIT: pass it only when the user explicitly limits where vendors ship from

shore_a.description: Numeric Shore A durometer ask (10-95, e.g. 40). Resolved to the NEAREST stocked durometer with a substitution note — never a silent swap

sides.description: single|double sided printing (defaults: cards double, flyers/posters single)

size.description: Print size — pass the user's words verbatim ("letter", "24x36", "half letter"). Cards are 3.5x2; flyers 8.5x5.5|8.5x11|11x17; posters 12x18 through 36x48. Unknown sizes get closest-match offers

tapping.description: Tapped (threaded) holes for a sheet-metal part — one record per hole the user wants threads cut into. `thread` is the callout in the user's words ("M6", "M4 x 0.7", "1/4-20") and is all that's required; when known, add the hole's center in the part's own mm frame (located_at_mm), its unit axis, the pre-tap drilled diameter, and depth_mm so the shop taps the right hole. Pass these when the user asks for threaded/tapped holes; vendors with a tapping service price them.

thickness_in.description: sheetmetal: Sheet thickness in inches (e.g. 0.063 = 14 ga aluminum). Quoted at the nearest stocked thickness; omit for ~16 ga default; laser_cut: Nominal thickness in inches; quoted at the vendor's nearest stocked thickness. Omit for the material's common stock

units.description: sheetmetal: DXF drawing units: "mm" (default) or "in". STEP files carry their own units; laser_cut: DXF drawing units: "mm" (default) or "in"

vendors.description: Only these specific vendors/makers ("just quote Slant 3D") — an INCLUDE list of vendor names as they appear on offers. Friendly names accepted ("A3D", "slant 3d"); unmatched names are reported, never an error. Usually OMIT: pass it only when the user explicitly names the vendors they want

vendors_exclude.description: Shops to leave out ("anyone but Slant 3D", "not A3D or Fictiv") — shop names as they appear on offers; friendly names accepted ("A3D", "slant 3d"), and a name that matches no shop is reported, never an error. A shop on this list is never asked and never shown. Works beside vendors: the shops shown are the vendors list (or everyone) minus this list, so a shop named on both is left out. Usually OMIT: pass it only when the user names shops they do not want

within_days.description: Arrival within this many calendar days from today ("within 10 days", "in two weeks" → 14). Counted from the day the quote is READ, so it keeps meaning "within N days of now" — the day is the UTC date, the one arrival dates on offers (eta_date) are written in, so compare against those dates rather than a local calendar; an option keeps only the shipping speeds that arrive in time. With deadline as well, the earlier date rules. Use deadline instead when the user names a date

tools.name: get_fabrication_quote
tools.title: Get fabrication quote

tools.description: Narrow an existing quote with new constraints (destination ZIP the user just provided, deadline, outdoor/waterproof/heat/food-safety requirements, budget, vendor reliability, verbatim requirements terms, drawing callouts, a process filter — "no, I meant in sheet metal" → processes — a ship-from country filter — "only US vendors" → ships_from — or a vendor filter — "only show A3D Manufacturing" → vendors) — or CHANGE its spec: material, color, or quantities. Changing material/quantity is a spec change, not a narrowing — pass it via the material/color/quantities args, NOT as a requirements term; the affected lanes re-price with the new spec through warm vendor sessions. For side-by-side comparisons ("how does carbon steel compare?"), add a scenario label — labeled refines coexist instead of replacing each other (max 4). "Organize by" ("sort by cheapest", "soonest arrival on top", "most green first") is also this tool: sort_by for objective orders, sort_order + sort_label for orders you judged yourself from the previews — presentation only, instant, nothing re-prices. GOING BACK is also this tool: undo_last_step ALONE takes back exactly one refine step (the quote's steps[] names each step, newest first — the network restores the previous stored state exactly); clear removes whole constraints ("drop the deadline" → clear ["deadline"]); remove_requirements takes back individual requirements terms. Call with ONLY quote_id to re-read the quote (e.g. to pick up preview images that finished rendering). TO PLACE EXACTLY ONE ORDER WITH NO MISTAKES: (1) on get_fabrication_quote list only that shop in vendors and state the pick in selection — the shop, plus the material, finish and shipping speed wanted; (2) read selection_match on the quote: status "one" means exactly one option answers the pick, "many" means say more in the pick (color, thickness, quantity), "none" means nothing on the quote answers it; (3) call create_checkout with quote_id and selection true — it orders that one option at the picked shipping speed, or refuses and creates nothing (selection_not_unique: the pick is not exactly one option; selection_speed_unavailable: the option does not show the picked speed now — an order never takes another speed in its place). It returns the payment link as always: the user pays on that page, nothing is charged without them. On a quote you already have, step (1) is this tool: refine_quote with vendors and selection. CHOOSING STARTS THAT SHOP'S CHECK: storing a pick that comes to exactly one option has that ONE shop asked to confirm it when its answer is more than 15 minutes old or was never given — only when the pick is all this call carries, or the pick now comes to a different option than before. The answer's selection_match.check says "running", "fresh" (nobody needed asking) or "not_started" with why. You do not have to wait: call create_checkout with quote_id and selection true next — it waits for that answer.

bend_count.description: How many bends this part has, when the user names a COUNT but not where the bends go ("it has 2 bends" → 2) — a spec change: sheet-metal lanes requote the part formed with that many bends (0 = cut it flat, on the record). The cheap acknowledgment for a flat design whose bends are not articulated: when a bends list is on the quote (or passed here), the list wins and this count follows it — change articulated bends through bends, not this. An earlier "cut it flat" (bends: null) does not pin the count: a later bend_count > 0 re-prices the part formed. Pass null to REMOVE a previously asked bend count — the part prices as if no count was ever stated

anyOf.description: Sheet-metal bend lines, each as TWO POINTS in the part's own mm frame (flat DXF parts use z=0: a bend from (0,12.7) to (76.2,12.7) is p1 [0,12.7,0], p2 [76.2,12.7,0]). angle_deg is the target bend angle (90 = a right-angle flange), direction "up"/"down" is the fold direction relative to the flat pattern, radius_mm the requested inside radius (omit it — the shop resolves to its tooling and reports what it used). Pass these when the user articulates WHERE the bends go; a bare "it has 2 bends" is bend_count, not this.

bends.description: New bend records for this part — a spec change: sheet lanes requote with exactly these bends (the list REPLACES the previous one, never patches it). Same shape as on get_fabrication_quote: each bend is two points in the part's own mm frame (flat DXF parts use z=0) plus angle_deg, direction up|down, and an optional requested radius_mm. Pass null to REMOVE every articulated bend

callouts.description: Dimensions you read off the user's drawing that matter ("hole_diameter 6.5mm ±0.1"). The tightest tolerance prunes vendors that cannot hold it.

cart_item_id.description: When the quote being changed is a part in a cart: that part's item_id from the cart. The cart then follows the part to the quote this call answers with, by itself. It changes nothing else about the call

clear.description: REMOVE constraints entirely ("drop the deadline", "forget the budget", "no more food-safe requirement"): list the constraints to clear and each is removed from the quote — the one deliberate widening besides undo. Clearing a deadline or budget answers instantly from held offers (near-misses convert back); clearing an attribute/reliability/requirements demand re-prices honestly. Same effect as ["any"] on the three filter args, extended to every constraint

color.description: New color for this part (spec change — lanes requote). Colour WORDS only ('black', 'green', 'clear'); the network resolves them to each maker's stocked shades, dyes, filaments or coatings — a family word ('blue') brings back EVERY stocked shade of it, and the quote's color_shades_available lists them — never pass a material or a shade you invented. Pass null to REMOVE a previously asked color — back to vendor defaults

color_shades.description: Narrow the board to these color SHADES exactly as the quote lists them (color_shades_available / "Colors on this board") — instant, nothing re-prices, the same quote id comes back with only those shades; pass null to show every shade again. Never invent a shade name.

deadline.description: Latest acceptable delivery date, ISO YYYY-MM-DD

finish.description: New surface finish ("powder coat", "anodized", "bead blasted") — a spec change: finish-capable lanes (sheet metal, CNC, metal print) requote WITH it; 3D-print lanes have no coating step, so they ignore the finish but keep the COLOR. A colored finish ask ("black powder coat") should set BOTH finish and color, so every lane lands on the buyer's color. Pass null to REMOVE a previously asked finish

anyOf.description: PEM-style hardware inserts pressed into holes of a sheet-metal part — one record per hole. `insert` is the species (nut | flush_nut | standoff | blind_standoff | stud) and `thread` its size ("M4", "1/4-20"); both are required. When known, add length_mm (standoff/stud post length), the hole's center (located_at_mm, part's own mm frame), its axis, the drilled diameter, and `points` — the signed unit vector the insert's functional side faces (flip = negate). Pass these when the user asks for press-in nuts/standoffs/studs; vendors with a hardware service price them.

inserts.description: New hardware-insert records for this part — a spec change: sheet lanes requote with exactly these inserts (the list REPLACES the previous one, never patches it). Same shape as on get_fabrication_quote: species (nut|flush_nut|standoff|blind_standoff|stud) and thread required, hole geometry optional. Pass null to REMOVE every insert

material.description: New material for this part ("I need it in PLA" → "pla"). A spec change: lanes requote with this material through warm vendor sessions; an explicit material here replaces the quote's material fan-out. Free-form — unstocked asks resolve to the closest stocked material with a substitution note. Do NOT pass material changes as requirements terms. Pass null to REMOVE a previously asked material ("forget the aluminum ask") — the ask comes off the record and the process-default material fan returns

materials.description: The materials the user will accept, when they name SEVERAL or a family rather than one ("plastic or metal", "delrin or PLA", "any aluminum") — each word a family ("plastic", "metal", "wood") or a specific material ("pla", "delrin", "aluminum_6061"). Only options in a listed material are shown; which shops are asked does not change. For ONE specific material use material instead: a stated material rules and this list is set aside (the quote says so). Usually OMIT: pass it only when the user names the materials they accept. On a refine: any list — narrower, wider, or clear ["materials"] to remove it — answers at once from what the quote holds (no shop is asked and nothing is priced again)

min_vendor_reviews.description: Only vendors with at least this many verified-purchase reviews

min_vendor_stars.description: Only vendors whose displayed review rating is at least this many stars (1-5); vendors with no reviews yet are excluded

on_behalf_of.description: Your own opaque name for the person you are acting for (a visitor id; never an email or a name), when you serve many people from one address: each then has their own count of the shop asks their choices start. It changes nothing else. Usually OMIT

processes.description: Narrow this quote to specific fabrication processes ("no, I meant in sheet metal" → ["sheet metal"]). A CONSTRAINT, not a new quote: excluded lanes drop while warm vendor sessions survive, and further refines inherit the filter. Friendly terms accepted ("sheet metal", "3d printing", "cnc", "laser"); pass ["any"] to clear the filter and show every process again. When comparison scenarios are open and the user narrows the process, re-refine EVERY active scenario label with this same arg so all columns prune together

proven_spec_orders.description: Only vendors with at least N completed orders for this exact process+material — "a vendor that prints PC reliably"

quantities.description: New quantities the user wants (spec change — lanes requote at the new quantity). Same rules as on get_fabrication_quote: pass the real ask, never inflate it. Pass null to REMOVE a previously asked quantity — the quote returns to single-part pricing

remove_requirements.description: Take back INDIVIDUAL requirements terms ("drop the anodized ask, keep the rest"): each listed term is removed from the quote's requirements by normalized match, the others stay. Unknown terms are ignored, never an error. Re-stating the requirements list can never drop a term (terms merge as a union) — this is the removal channel

requirements.description: Verbatim context terms from the user — materials, finishes, certifications, tolerances ("UV resistant", "anodized: red", "iso 13485", "tolerance: 0.1mm"). UFP applies what it can and reports what it could not; unresolvable terms are logged for vendor sourcing. Do not interrogate the user to fill this — pass what they said.

scale.description: Rescale the DESIGN ITSELF before re-quoting: per-axis stretch factors over the file's current geometry ("make it 2x bigger" = {"x":2,"y":2,"z":2}). Mesh designs are genuinely converted — the child quote prices a rescaled file; STEP/IGES designs keep their original file with the dimensions riding as callouts (pass those too). {1,1,1} is a no-op

scenario.description: Comparison lane label. A labeled refine sits SIDE BY SIDE with the quote's other offers instead of replacing them: refines with the same label replace that scenario, different labels coexist (max 4 per quote), and a refine WITHOUT a scenario resets the baseline and supersedes every lane. Friendly terms accepted ("US", "Europe", "Germany", "China", "UK"). Vendors whose origin is unknown or whose network is worldwide (a specific origin cannot be guaranteed) are excluded, each with an honest note. For "nothing from X" asks, pass the regions the user does want instead

tools.description: INTERNAL client rail — the routing half of refine_quote with NOTHING committed: takes the same arguments as refine_quote and answers how many distinct fabricators (and which process lanes) the network WOULD ask for the refined part, plus the exclusion notes, without creating a child quote, asking any vendor, superseding in-flight work, or logging demand. bends.description: New bend records for this part — a spec change: sheet lanes requote with exactly these bends (the list REPLACES the previous one, never patches it). tools.name: preview_quote
tools.title: Preview quote routing (soft quote)

tools.description: Use when the user comes back to a part priced earlier (a saved quote_id), or when a quote carried answers_pending. A quote's answers are shown for 24 hours. Inside them this returns the same quote and asks nobody (reopened "same"). Past them it makes a NEW quote of the same file, configuration, rules and pick — work from the quote_id it returns: with the answers anyone got for this same part and request in the last 24 hours ("copied", nobody asked); else by asking the shops once ("asked" — the offers fill in like any new quote); else, when someone is asking about it right now, at our instant prices ("waiting": call this again after answers_pending.retry_after_s seconds). "press_needed" = this quote was itself made by reopening an old one and nothing was picked or changed on it since, so nobody is asked again by itself: pass pressed true only when the user asks for today's prices. A quote of a shared cart, a part already paid for, or instant prices only comes back as it reads. Do not use it to look at a board again. HOW OLD AN ANSWER IS: a shop's answer is shown for 24 hours, to everyone with the same request (the same design bytes with the same everything asked), so a quote of a part someone priced in the last 24 hours comes back complete at once with those answers and no shop is asked again. An offer says when its shop answered (answered_at). Past 15 minutes it reads stale: true — it is shown at that price and the shop confirms it again before anyone pays (check_offer, or checking out, asks that one shop). A shipping option of such an offer carries eta_approximate: true: say "about N days" from eta_days and never state its eta_date as a date, because no shop stands behind a date until it confirms again. If a quote carries answers_pending, someone else is asking the shops about this same request right now and these are our instant prices: call reopen_quote with that quote_id after retry_after_s seconds.

pressed.description: true = the user asked for today's prices. Needed only after reopened read "press_needed"

tools.name: reopen_quote
tools.title: Reopen a quote someone came back to

tools.description: INTERNAL — the offer board calls this to refresh itself while vendors finish pricing. Never call this yourself. The board you were given is already final for its turn; do not reach for refine_quote to look at it again either, that paints a duplicate board. An offer's manufacturability_check (status checking → passed | failed, expected_s; "repriced" reads as passed) means the price is set; the shop is confirming it can make the part as drawn; the board renders it.

quote_id.description: Quote id the board is watching

tools.name: poll_quote
tools.title: Poll quote (board internal)

tools.description: ONLY for the case where a quote response came back with an EMPTY board and told you to call this: waits for the vendors to answer (up to ~40s) and returns their offers as a full board. Call with just quote_id, immediately, and say nothing substantive before it. NEVER call it on a response that already listed offers — that board is final, and this would add nothing.

quote_id.description: Quote id from the still-quoting response

tools.name: finalize_quote
tools.title: Finalize quote (wait for remaining vendors)

tools.description: Create the order and get a hosted payment link for a chosen offer. Call this as soon as the user picks an offer + shipping speed. This tool takes NO personal details: never ask for — and never pass — a name, address, email, or phone; the secure payment page collects the shipping address, email, and phone (and billing) itself, even when the user volunteered them in chat. Returns checkout_url — AFN's order page (what is being made, by which shop, the all-in price) with a Continue to payment button to the secure hosted payment page; give the link to the user. UFP places the vendor order automatically after payment. An offer whose shop still has to confirm it (manufacturability_check.status "unchecked", or confirmed more than 15 minutes ago) is confirmed by this call itself, and one whose status is "checking" is waited for (the price is set; the shop is confirming it can make the part as drawn) — no separate check_offer call. Pass max_total_cents: the price the user agreed to (the offer's subtotal_cents plus the chosen shipping cost_cents). THE CHECKOUT RULE, enforced by the network for every client: an offer can be ordered only when the shop's own system has accepted this part at this price — its manufacturability check has passed, the price is the shop's own number (price_basis "vendor_api"), and no price confirmation is outstanding. That acceptance is good for 15 minutes (the offer's confirmed_until). THE CHECKOUT CONFIRMS WHAT NEEDS CONFIRMING ITSELF: when the option's shop has not confirmed it, or did more than 15 minutes ago, the checkout asks that ONE shop (it joins the ask already running when choosing the option started one) and waits up to wait_s for the answer; when the wait runs out first the answer is offer_not_ready with retry_after_s — send the SAME call again, it joins the ask and nothing is asked twice. THE PAY RULE: the same or a lower price goes straight to the payment link; a price the shop confirmed HIGHER than the user agreed to stops ONCE (price_went_up, with old_total_cents and new_total_cents) and nothing is created — tell the user both figures, then send the call again (with the new max_total_cents when you sent one); the new price stands for 15 minutes and no shop is asked again. A passed offer whose price_refresh is still "pending" is refused the same way (offer_not_ready, with retry_after_s): the shop is still confirming its price — re-read the quote and retry then. An offer whose check failed, whose price_refresh reads "failed", or whose fulfillment is "not_connected" cannot be ordered at all (offer_check_failed) — offer the user another option or re-quote. Nothing is charged on any refusal. An offer whose shop could not confirm the part — it declined the part, or did not answer within two minutes of being asked — leaves the quote: it is no longer listed in offers, and its id is refused the same way. If an offer you showed earlier is missing when you re-read the quote, tell the user plainly that the shop could not confirm the part, and carry on with the offers that are listed. ORDER BY THE PICK: instead of offer_id + shipping_option_id, pass quote_id with selection true to order the one option the quote's stored pick comes to (the quote's selection_match). It orders only when that reads status "one"; with none or several it is refused (selection_not_unique, saying how many matched) and nothing is created — say more in the pick with refine_quote selection, then call again. When the pick names a shipping speed the option does not show right now (selection_match.speed_fallback) it is refused too (selection_speed_unavailable): the cheapest speed is never ordered in its place — store the pick with a speed the option lists. An offer_id or shipping speed the quote's own rules keep off its board (the acceptable-materials list, within_days) is refused the same way: order what the quote lists now. So the whole of it is two calls: refine_quote with the pick (its one shop starts confirming), then create_checkout with quote_id and selection true — a payment link, or price_went_up once, or offer_not_ready (call again). The checkout rule above applies to the picked option exactly as to any other. Keep the optional comment to a short factual summary of their words; never embellish. ALWAYS draft the review (stars, facets, comment) and confirm it with the user BEFORE calling this tool — e.g. "I'll rate this 2 stars with timeliness 1 because it arrived 2 days late — send it?". One review per order: submitting again updates the existing review. If you do not have the order id from this conversation, ask the user for it (it is on their receipt email and order page); never guess one.

tools.description: Run the shop's manufacturability check on ONE offer whose manufacturability_check.status is "unchecked" (the price stands from the shop's own pricing, but no shop was asked for that material / finish yet) or still "checking". The network asks that shop once for exactly this option — its material, gauge, finish, quantity and the quote's destination — and lands the answer on the SAME offer: passed (orderable at the shown price; a status of "repriced" means exactly the same — the price shown is the shop's, never tell the user it changed) or failed (the shop could not confirm the part: the offer cannot be ordered and is no longer listed on the quote — the answer still carries it, with a plain message; tell the user and carry on with the offers that are listed). Call it when the user settles on such an offer and before create_checkout (checkout refuses an unchecked offer). Waits up to wait_s (default 45) for the shop; pending: true means the shop is still answering — re-read the quote shortly. Nothing else on the quote changes. On an instant-only quote (routing.instant_only true) no shop is asked: the offer comes back unchanged with a plain message — relay it, and quote the part again without instant_only if the user wants to order. On a lazy quote (routing.lazy true) this call is how a shop is asked at all: it asks the one shop of this offer, and the offer can be ordered once it passes. A shop's confirmation of an offer is good for 15 minutes: while it stands the offer carries confirmed_until (an ISO time) and can be ordered. After it the offer is NOT failed and NOT removed — it keeps its place and the price the shop last confirmed, and its manufacturability_check reads status "unchecked" with reason "confirmation_lapsed". CHOOSING STARTS THAT SHOP'S CHECK: when the user settles on an option and you store the pick, that one shop is asked again by itself (the answer's selection_match.check reads "running"), and create_checkout and checkout_cart ask it themselves too when it still needs confirming — nobody else is asked, and no separate check_offer call is needed. Pay when it lands: the checkout waits for it. If the shop's price came back higher than the user agreed to, the checkout stops ONCE (price_went_up, with the old and the new figure) and nothing is created: tell the user both figures, then send the same call again. An offer whose manufacturability_check reads status "unchecked" with reason "network_restarted" was being confirmed by its shop when the network restarted, so the answer never came: tell the user, in these words, "A new version of AFN has been released, please refresh the page". Nothing is lost — the price stands and the offer can simply be checked again with check_offer. Say it once, when a tool's own text tells you to; the same reason still on an offer on a later read is history, not news.
